chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Luck of recording and the lack of names on records
summary: Whether you got on a record was luck, and early records did not list the sidemen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I guess sometimes it's a matter of luck, too; at least it was those days. If you happened to be with a band that got to record and the records were on a label that would get around a little bit, that would make a difference.
Yes. These days... I don't think they're putting names of guys on records no more, do they? Not much.
Well, they put it on the folder. But when you get to the record... Suppose the folder gets lost. You got a record you don't know who plays what. You know?
Well, but now they've got all these discographies and everything...
Yeah. Well, but you know, so a guy has got to play some more money to...
It took a long time to find out who played on all those early things, because...
I know it! I know it, because they didn't put no names. You know, just the guy who made the record. Yeah, man, so that's how it is, you know...
